newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Disgruntled PAL workers ask Ramos' help.
newsitem.headline: Disgruntled PAL workers ask Ramos' help.

text.p: Disgruntled Philippine Airlines (PAL) workers urged President Fidel Ramos on Tuesday to intervene in a brewing labour dispute to avert a possible airline strike before the APEC summit next month.

"We are pleading for ... your timely intervention to douse the fuming anger of our members which (we) strongly feel might trigger a timely mass action," the three PAL labour unions said in a letter to Ramos, copies of which were released to media.

The unions -- the PAL Employees Association, the Flight Attendants and Stewards Association of the Philippines, and the Air Line Pilots Association of the Philippines -- are asking for negotiations on new wage package worth 3.2 billion pesos ($121 million) over the next two years.
PAL has rejected the package and instead offered to sell PAL shares worth 477 million pesos ($18.15 million) at five pesos (19 cents) per share to its employees.

"The stock offering will partially meet the cash component of the economic benefits demanded by the three PAL labour unions even while the airline is cash-strapped and continues to incur losses at approximately 3.0 million pesos ($114,133) a day that could reach more than one billion pesos ($38 million) by the end of the current fiscal year," the company said in a statement.
PAL has incurred net losses in the past several years due to high operating expenses and cutthroat competition in international routes.

The unions rejected the stock offer and filed a notice of strike with the Department of Labour and Employment two weeks ago under a law requiring unions to obtain state clearance before staging walkouts.
The department rejected the unions' petition, saying a strike before the scheduled November 25 summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum would embarrass the country.
PAL workers said they had no intention of embarrassing the government and have started a work slowdown which PAL management said had delayed some domestic flights.
PAL senior vice president Antonio Ocampo said contingency measures had been set up in case of a full-blown stoppage.
The measures include reducing flights on routes where the competition operates.
Aside from the proposed wage package, the workers were also complaining about illegal termination of union officers and members and rampant use of contractual workers.
